record.text: Which EU-funded projects put in place, as part of their own work, engineered planted treatment systems for wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - beds, ponds or modules filled with gravel, sand or soil and planted with vegetation, through which the water to be cleaned is passed so that the plants and the microbes around their roots do the treating with little or no energy input? I mean a unit the project itself builds, operates or tests during the grant, not natural marshes being studied or restored, and not planted drainage features installed to manage rainwater runoff for flood or heat resilience.
record.reference_answer: Fifteen EU-funded projects build, run or test such a unit. A decentralised, near-zero-energy sewage strand is the largest: iMETland built a full-scale device to treat urban wastewater from small communities at zero-energy operation cost by combining electroactive bacteria and an electroconductive material with the biofilter bed, reaching depuration rates 10-fold higher than classical techniques; ELECTRAMMOX extends that METland concept to anaerobic ammonium oxidation for N removal from sewage; ELECTRA ran electrochemically enhanced versions that improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw or secondary treated municipal wastewater; and alchemia-nova's VertECO work develops indoor and outdoor plant-based units for household grey-water. Others target a named contaminant or water source: ZIRONITRO's planted ponds remove nitrate from groundwater (98% removal, 84% lower cost than current solutions), TOXICROP reports toxic cyanobacteria clearance rates on the order of 94% and about 99% removal rates of the toxin microcystins, INDIA-H2O validated phyto-treatment in a small wetland construction and then a larger constructed system for saline groundwater and industrial wastewater in Gujarat, and M2EX used such beds to polish bioleaching effluent until it was suitable for irrigation. The rest embed them in larger treatment trains: AquaNES combines them with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, HYDROUSA couples them with anaerobic processes and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection, INCOVER runs them as one of the resource-recovery technologies validated at demo scale in Spain and Germany, PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands+' in real Indian environments, MULTISOURCE monitored seven such pilots for wastewater parameters, microplastics and pathogens, NICE constructed 15 pilots across 10 urban sites covering wastewater, greywater and combined sewer overflow, and WATERAGRI tested farm-scale versions for water quality and nutrient recovery from agricultural catchments.
record.notes: Membership test, stated in the question text and applied in both directions in one pass: the project ITSELF builds, operates or tests a planted treatment unit (bed, pond or module of gravel/sand/soil with vegetation) during the grant, and the water passed through it is wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - not natural marshes studied or restored, and not planted drainage features for rainwater runoff managed for flood or heat resilience. Seeds: the six projects whose objective/title carry the specialist label (642190, 689450, 701542, 773351, 858375, 894525); drift check re-executed and returned exactly those six. FIX ROUND CHANGES. (1) 854782 M-NBS removed from gold: its whole workPerformed is commercial ('During Phase 1 we have carried out a thorough market analysis to select our target countries ... a well-defined commercial strategy ... confirmed our Freedom to Operate and analyzed the relevant regulation concerning the transport of our modules ... rethought our supply chain'), and the deployments its objective claims predate the grant ('has been successfully applied NBS in more than 100 large scale natural sanitation and remediation projects as non-mobile unit'). No unit built or operated under the grant is stated, so it fails the physical test. (2) 101000348 DIVAGRI re-argued against the sentence the critic named rather than against its framing: it PASSES the own-work half of the test ('Biotechnologies co-developed with smallholders at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites ... include ... artificial wetland'; 'All seven bio-based technologies will be installed at all pilot sites within the next few months'), and is excluded only on the water half - the sole sentence assigning that unit a duty calls it a water SAVING technology ('Water saving technologies such as artificial wetlands and a sub-surface clay-based irrigation system have already caught the attention of farmers') and no polluted water stream is named anywhere in its text. (3) The water being treated is now in the question text, so 730283 GROW GREEN is decided on text a system sees: its constructed features are raingardens, swales, tree pits, permeable pavements and infiltration trenches created to 'adapt cityscapes to a climate change', in cities that 'already experience flooding and heat stress' - runoff managed for flood and heat resilience, excluded. Rain-garden / bioretention / swale / SuDS sweep (objective + all report sections, terms: rain garden, raingarden, swale, bioretention, bio-retention, sustainable urban drainage, SuDS) returned 11 projects, all adjudicated: 101003765 NICE IN (see below), 730283 GROW GREEN OUT (runoff for climate resilience), 786566 Mind4Stormwater OUT (asset MANAGEMENT of existing stormwater control measures - 'their long-term management is far from assured' - builds nothing and the water is stormwater), 641931 CENTAUR OUT (real-time control of sewer networks to reduce urban flood risk; no planted unit), 101008626 Co-UDlabs OUT (transnational access to urban-drainage research facilities), 867798 Bufferblock OUT (plastic/concrete drainage blocks under roads for buffering, no vegetation), and 633125 EUCYS 2014, 754475 HD-App, 947761 AGING MATTERS, 101028810 ATTENTIVE, 101031317 EstroGen, 101036560 REGILIENCE OUT as substring false matches with no water-treatment content. why_good: The question discriminates on whether a system can find a technology described only by its physical mechanism when the corpus always names it with one specialist label the question never uses, and then on two separations that share almost all of that vocabulary: built treatment units versus natural marshes studied or restored, and planted units treating polluted water versus planted drainage features handling rainwater runoff. It fills the environmental-engineering / water-treatment axis at L3 with term_style=paraphrase, which the existing vector set carries only at vec-05 on a different topic. The L3 label is arithmetic: 15 gold projects, each with a quoted sentence showing the project itself builds, operates or tests such a unit on polluted water, and 8 of the 15 have that sentence only in report_text.

record.text: Which EU-funded projects put in place, as part of their own work, engineered planted treatment systems for wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - beds, ponds or modules filled with gravel, sand or soil and planted with vegetation, through which the water to be cleaned is passed so that the plants and the microbes around their roots do the treating with little or no energy input? I mean a unit the project itself builds, operates or tests during the grant, not natural marshes being studied or restored, and not planted drainage features installed to manage rainwater runoff for flood or heat resilience.
record.reference_answer: Fifteen EU-funded projects build, run or test such a unit. A decentralised, near-zero-energy sewage strand is the largest: iMETland built a full-scale device to treat urban wastewater from small communities at zero-energy operation cost by combining electroactive bacteria and an electroconductive material with the biofilter bed, reaching depuration rates 10-fold higher than classical techniques; ELECTRAMMOX extends that METland concept to anaerobic ammonium oxidation for N removal from sewage; ELECTRA ran electrochemically enhanced versions that improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw or secondary treated municipal wastewater; and alchemia-nova's VertECO work develops indoor and outdoor plant-based units for household grey-water. Others target a named contaminant or water source: ZIRONITRO's planted ponds remove nitrate from groundwater (98% removal, 84% lower cost than current solutions), TOXICROP reports toxic cyanobacteria clearance rates on the order of 94% and about 99% removal rates of the toxin microcystins, INDIA-H2O validated phyto-treatment in a small wetland construction and then a larger constructed system for saline groundwater and industrial wastewater in Gujarat, and M2EX used such beds to polish bioleaching effluent until it was suitable for irrigation. The rest embed them in larger treatment trains: AquaNES combines them with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, HYDROUSA couples them with anaerobic processes and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection, INCOVER runs them as one of the resource-recovery technologies validated at demo scale in Spain and Germany, PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands+' in real Indian environments, MULTISOURCE monitored seven such pilots for wastewater parameters, microplastics and pathogens, NICE constructed 15 pilots across 10 urban sites covering wastewater, greywater and combined sewer overflow, and WATERAGRI tested farm-scale versions for water quality and nutrient recovery from agricultural catchments.
record.notes: Membership test, stated in the question text and applied in both directions in one pass: the project ITSELF builds, operates or tests a planted treatment unit (bed, pond or module of gravel/sand/soil with vegetation) during the grant, and the water passed through it is wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - not natural marshes studied or restored, and not planted drainage features for rainwater runoff managed for flood or heat resilience. record.text: Which EU-funded projects put in place, as part of their own work, engineered planted treatment systems for wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - beds, ponds or modules filled with gravel, sand or soil and planted with vegetation, through which the water to be cleaned is passed so that the plants and the microbes around their roots do the treating with little or no energy input? I mean a unit the project itself builds, operates or tests during the grant, not natural marshes being studied or restored, and not planted drainage features installed to manage rainwater runoff for flood or heat resilience.
record.reference_answer: Fifteen EU-funded projects build, run or test such a unit. A decentralised, near-zero-energy sewage strand is the largest: iMETland built a full-scale device to treat urban wastewater from small communities at zero-energy operation cost by combining electroactive bacteria and an electroconductive material with the biofilter bed, reaching depuration rates 10-fold higher than classical techniques; ELECTRAMMOX extends that METland concept to anaerobic ammonium oxidation for N removal from sewage; ELECTRA ran electrochemically enhanced versions that improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw or secondary treated municipal wastewater; and alchemia-nova's VertECO work develops indoor and outdoor plant-based units for household grey-water. Others target a named contaminant or water source: ZIRONITRO's planted ponds remove nitrate from groundwater (98% removal, 84% lower cost than current solutions), TOXICROP reports toxic cyanobacteria clearance rates on the order of 94% and about 99% removal rates of the toxin microcystins, INDIA-H2O validated phyto-treatment in a small wetland construction and then a larger constructed system for saline groundwater and industrial wastewater in Gujarat, and M2EX used such beds to polish bioleaching effluent until it was suitable for irrigation. The rest embed them in larger treatment trains: AquaNES combines them with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, HYDROUSA couples them with anaerobic processes and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection, INCOVER runs them as one of the resource-recovery technologies validated at demo scale in Spain and Germany, PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands+' in real Indian environments, MULTISOURCE monitored seven such pilots for wastewater parameters, microplastics and pathogens, NICE constructed 15 pilots across 10 urban sites covering wastewater, greywater and combined sewer overflow, and WATERAGRI tested farm-scale versions for water quality and nutrient recovery from agricultural catchments.
record.notes: Membership test, stated in the question text and applied in both directions in one pass: the project ITSELF builds, operates or tests a planted treatment unit (bed, pond or module of gravel/sand/soil with vegetation) during the grant, and the water passed through it is wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - not natural marshes studied or restored, and not planted drainage features for rainwater runoff managed for flood or heat resilience. The L3 label is arithmetic: 15 gold projects, each with a quoted sentence showing the project itself builds, operates or tests such a unit on polluted water, and 8 of the 15 have that sentence only in report_text.
